$metadata.description: Extract regulatory requirements from geothermal ordinances

normalization.description: State names automatically normalized to 2-letter abbreviations (e.g., Utah→UT, New York→NY) during consolidation for consistent data analysis

title: Geothermal Electricity Ordinance Extraction Schema
description: Regulatory requirements for geothermal electricity generation facilities. SCOPE: Geothermal power plants, geothermal production/injection wells for electricity, commercial geothermal energy facilities. EXCLUDE: Geothermal heat pumps (GHP), residential HVAC, direct-use heating/cooling, solar power, wind power, biomass, and other non-geothermal energy technologies. CRITICAL: When extracting from multi-technology renewable energy ordinances, DO NOT extract requirements that apply to solar, wind, biomass, or other technologies. ONLY extract provisions that explicitly mention geothermal or that clearly apply to geothermal based on context.

applies_to_geothermal_electricity.description: Does this document contain provisions regulating geothermal electricity generation?

extraction_approach.description: Document which sections were extracted (geothermal-related) and which were excluded (other technologies/uses). IMPORTANT: If document is a zoning code that lists geothermal as a permitted/conditional use in certain zones, extract ONLY: (1) The geothermal use classification itself, (2) Zone-specific requirements (setbacks, lot size, etc.) from zones where geothermal is allowed. EXCLUDE: Requirements for other land uses (residential, guest houses, manufactured homes, accessory buildings) even if on the same page. For multi-technology renewable energy ordinances, ONLY extract sections that explicitly mention geothermal - DO NOT extract general 'renewable energy' sections that apply to all technologies including solar/wind/biomass. Use format: 'Extracted [sections]; Excluded [sections]'
examples: Extracted Article N.G Sections 6-3N-1 through 6-3N-12 (geothermal); Excluded Section 6-4-12G (solar), Section 6-3C-2 (residential GHP)
Extracted Division 17 (commercial geothermal); Excluded general zoning provisions

Extracted Table of Uses (geothermal power plant classification) and I-A zone site development standards (applicable to geothermal); Excluded R4K residential standards, guest house regulations, manufactured home definitions
No geothermal electricity provisions found; Excluded all sections (document covers only solar and wind)

relevant_sections.description: Ordinance sections regulating geothermal electricity, cited exactly as written (e.g., 'Article N.G Sections 6-3N-1 through 6-3N-12'). Null if none.

state.description: State name exactly as written in document.

county.description: County name exactly as written (keep 'County' suffix if present).

ordinance_code.description: Ordinance number/code/title exactly as written. Null if not stated.

date_adopted.description: Date the ordinance was adopted/enacted/passed by the legislative body in YYYY-MM-DD format. Convert from any source format (e.g., 'May 17, 2013' → '2013-05-17', 'October 6, 2015' → '2015-10-06', '10/6/2015' → '2015-10-06'). Look for phrases like 'adopted on', 'enacted on', 'passed on', or dates in resolution headers. If year-only (e.g., '2015'), use 'YYYY-01-01' format. For descriptive dates (e.g., 'upon approval'), keep original text. Null if not stated.

date_effective.description: Date the ordinance became effective/applicable law in YYYY-MM-DD format. Convert from any source format to YYYY-MM-DD. This may differ from adoption date. Look for phrases like 'effective date', 'shall become effective on', 'in effect as of'. For descriptive effective dates (e.g., 'immediately upon adoption', 'upon Board approval'), keep original text as-is rather than converting. Null if not stated.

date_last_amended.description: Date of the most recent amendment to the ordinance in YYYY-MM-DD format. Convert from any source format (e.g., '1-29-2013' → '2013-01-29', 'January 29, 2013' → '2013-01-29'). Look for phrases like 'amended on', 'as amended', 'last revised'. Null if not stated or if no amendments.

supersedes.description: Previous ordinance/resolution that this ordinance replaces or supersedes, exactly as written. Look for phrases like 'replaces', 'supersedes', 'repeals and replaces'. Null if not stated.

requirements.description: Regulatory requirements applicable to geothermal electricity facilities. CRITICAL EXTRACTION RULES: (1) ONE-TO-MANY RULE: When a single regulation applies to multiple subjects/boundaries/entities/activities, create SEPARATE rows for each. Example: 'Setback from property lines, roads, and water bodies shall be 100 feet' → Create 3 rows with different specific_subject values ('from property line', 'from public roads', 'from water bodies'). Example: 'Working hours restricted to 7 AM - 7 PM for site preparation, equipment delivery, and drill pipe racking' → Create 3 rows with different specific_subject values ('site preparation', 'equipment delivery and removal', 'drill pipe racking'). (2) ALTERNATIVE VALUES RULE: When a regulation offers multiple options (either/or scenarios), create separate rows for each option, marking each with value_type='alternative_option'. Example: '$50k per well OR $150k blanket bond' → 2 rows with different specific_subject and value fields. (3) BUNDLED CRITERIA RULE: When a section lists multiple distinct requirements, extract EACH as a SEPARATE row with appropriate category. DO NOT combine into summary rows. Break down numbered/lettered subsections into individual requirements with specific categories like 'Setback', 'Waste disposal', 'Zero discharge system', 'Noise limit', 'Working hours restricted', 'Lighting', etc. (4) CRITICAL FILTERING: DO NOT extract requirements mentioning 'solar', 'wind', 'biomass', or other non-geothermal technologies.

category.description: Broad type of regulatory requirement. Use general, reusable categories. For setbacks, use 'Setback' (not 'Setback from X' - that goes in specific_subject). For limits, use 'Height limit', 'Noise limit', etc. The category should be generic enough that similar requirements across jurisdictions share the same category value, enabling cross-jurisdiction comparison.

specific_subject.description: The specific target, boundary, activity, or scope that distinguishes this instance of the requirement from others in the same category. CRITICAL: This field should make each row unique within its category. EXAMPLES BY CATEGORY: (1) Setbacks → 'from property line', 'from public road right-of-way', 'from residential structures', 'from water bodies', 'from schools', 'from hospitals'. (2) Bonds → 'per well', 'blanket bond for all wells'. (3) Height limits → 'cooling tower', 'wellhead structure', 'transmission tower'. (4) Noise limits → 'at property line', 'at nearest residence', 'construction equipment', 'well venting and testing'. (5) Working hours restricted → 'site preparation', 'equipment delivery and removal', 'drill pipe racking', 'well venting'. (6) Operational requirements → specify the equipment/process/activity being regulated. RULE: When one regulation mentions multiple targets/activities (e.g., 'setback from property lines, roads, and tanks' OR 'working hours for site prep, delivery, and drilling'), create separate rows with different specific_subject values. Set to null only if the requirement truly has no sub-categorization.

applies_to.description: What entity, equipment, or operation this requirement regulates. Use the actual terminology from the ordinance. IMPORTANT: For zone-based requirements (from zoning codes), specify the zone context if geothermal is allowed in specific zones only (e.g., 'Geothermal power plants in I-A zone', 'Geothermal facilities in A-20 zone'). For universal requirements, use 'Geothermal power plant' or 'All geothermal facilities'. Set to null if the requirement applies broadly or if not specified.
examples: Geothermal power plants in I-A zone

value.description: The primary quantifiable value extracted from the requirement. EXTRACTION RULES: (1) FIXED NUMBERS: For simple numeric requirements, extract the number without units (e.g., '1320 feet' → 1320, value_type='fixed_number'). (2) FORMULAS: For calculated values, extract the complete formula as a string (e.g., '1.5 times the total height of its tallest cooling tower or highest structure', value_type='formula'). Do NOT attempt to calculate or simplify formulas. (3) RANGES: For ranges, extract as string (e.g., '100-500 feet', '7 a.m. to 7 p.m.', value_type='range'). (4) YES/NO: Extract 'Required', 'Mandatory', 'Prohibited', 'Not permitted' as appropriate. (5) ALTERNATIVES: When regulation offers either/or options, create separate rows with different values and value_type='alternative_option'. (6) Use null only if the requirement is pure procedural text with no extractable quantifiable element.
examples: 1.5 times the total height of its tallest cooling tower or highest structure
2 times the height but not less than 500 feet

value_type.description: Categorizes how the value should be interpreted. TYPES: 'fixed_number' = simple numeric value (default, can be null); 'formula' = calculated value with variables (e.g., '2x height'); 'range' = min-max or time range; 'alternative_option' = one of multiple either/or choices in the regulation; 'tiered' = value varies by facility size/capacity/other factor; 'minimum' = explicitly a floor; 'maximum' = explicitly a ceiling. USE CASES: (1) Set to 'formula' when value contains calculations like 'X times Y' or 'X% of Y'. (2) Set to 'alternative_option' when the regulation says 'either X or Y' - create separate rows for each option. (3) Set to 'tiered' when requirements vary by conditions (pair with 'condition' field). (4) Set to null or 'fixed_number' for straightforward numeric values.

unit.description: Unit of measurement SPELLED OUT in full words - NEVER use symbols or abbreviations unless standard. EXTRACTION RULES: (1) For distances → Use 'feet' not "'" or "′", 'meters' not 'm', 'mile' not 'mi'. (2) For noise → Use 'dBA' (standard abbreviation OK). (3) For area → Use 'acres' or 'square feet' spelled out. (4) For currency → Use 'USD' or '$' as written. (5) For time periods → Spell out (e.g., 'days', 'calendar days', 'years'). (6) Use null if: value is null, value is yes/no, value is a time range, or value_type is 'formula' (formula expressions include their own units). CRITICAL: If document shows "'", "′", or "ft" → extract as 'feet'. If document shows '"' or "″" → extract as 'inches'.

condition.description: Additional qualifying conditions that modify when or how the requirement applies. Captures temporal, spatial, capacity-based, or other contextual constraints. EXAMPLES: Temporal → 'during daytime hours (7 AM - 7 PM)', 'during construction phase', 'during nighttime hours'. Capacity-based → 'for facilities exceeding 25 MW', 'for first 10 MW of capacity', 'if total site area exceeds 100 acres'. Spatial → 'when located within 1 mile of residential areas', 'except in industrial zones', 'in agricultural districts'. Equipment-specific → 'during drilling operations', 'while turbines are operating'. Alternative scopes → 'for each well drilled or abandoned well re-entered', 'for any number of wells drilled or re-entered'. RULE: Use this field to capture the qualifying context that distinguishes otherwise similar requirements. For tiered or alternative_option value_type, this field should specify the tier/option criteria. Set to null if the requirement has no additional conditions.
examples: when located within 1 mile of residential areas
for each well drilled or abandoned well re-entered
for any number of wells drilled or re-entered
if total site area exceeds 100 acres

details.description: Complete requirement text verbatim from the ordinance. Include all conditions, exceptions, qualifications, and contextual language. EXTRACTION RULE: Copy the full legal text exactly as written - this preserves the complete regulatory language. The 'value' and 'unit' fields extract the KEY quantifiable elements for analysis, while this field preserves the full regulatory context.

section.description: Ordinance section reference as cited in document (e.g., '6-3N-10-1C', 'Section 10-404(2)(c)'). Null if no section numbering.
